lesson.title: Blanks, zeros and repeats
lesson.subtitle: A blank is not a zero, repeats, and checks with a cleaning log

video.title: Blanks, zeros and repeats
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria, runs the weather club (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: A blank is not a zero

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Over 200 mm?; A dry river; 999: an error code. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our rain report said Riverside had more than two hundred millimetres in a week. The river was nearly dry! One gauge had sent nine nine nine, its error code.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: blanks, zeros and repeats, and the checks that catch them.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “0” (Read, and it was dry) and “Blank” (Nobody read it; Absent? Not marked? Forgotten?).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A blank is not a zero
scenes.narration: A blank is not a zero. Zero rain means the gauge was read, and it was dry. A blank means nobody read it. And for a pupil's mark, a blank might mean absent, not yet marked, or simply forgotten.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: As zero: the average drops; As present: looks too good; Leave it out, and say so.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So never fill a blank silently. Count it as zero, and the average drops; count it as present, and attendance looks better than it was. Leave it out, count how many, and say so in your report.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Same pupil, same day, twice; Clean the names first; “Amina” and “Aminah”.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Repeats are rows typed twice: the same pupil, on the same day. But they only show up once the names agree. Amina on Monday and Aminah on Monday look like two pupils until you clean the names.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: In range: 0 to 300 mm; Not empty; No repeats; Only names on the list.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A check: a rule every row passes
scenes.narration: A check is a rule every row must pass. In range: rain from zero to three hundred millimetres. Not empty. No repeats. And only names that are on the list.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Stop the batch; Set bad rows aside; Let it through, warn; Write it in the log.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When a check fails, you decide. Stop the whole batch, set the bad rows aside, or let them through with a warning. Either way, write it in your cleaning log: what, where, what you did, and why.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! One pupil's mark is blank. When I work out the class average, what should I do with it?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: As zero: too low; Filled in: invented; Left out, and said.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Leave it out, and say so
scenes.narration: Leave it out, and say that one mark is missing. Counting it as zero pulls the average down, and filling in the average invents a mark nobody earned.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: seen = set() … Caption: Station and day together: one reading each
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Python can check every row for you. To find repeats, keep a set of what you've seen: the station and the day together. If a row's pair is already there, it's a repeat.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: 4 clubs, 5 batches; Turn checks on; All off: 6 stations!.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, four weather clubs send rain readings every evening. Turn the checks on and off, and choose what happens when one fails. With every check off, the report shows six stations instead of four.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A batch has one bad reading among twenty good ones. Which choice keeps the good data moving?

scenes.visual: Summary card: A blank is not a zero; Names first, then repeats; Checks on every batch; Log every change. Takeaway bar: Clean data says what was done to it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Set the bad row aside, and send it back to the club to fix. Remember: a blank is not a zero, so never fill it silently. Clean the names before you look for repeats. And check every batch, and log what you changed.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A rain table, four problems; Groups find them; Decide, then log it. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Data detective”. Give groups a paper rain table with four hidden problems: a blank, a nine nine nine, a minus sign and a repeat. They find them, decide what to do, and write a cleaning log.

checkpoints.prompt: One pupil's mark is blank. When you work out the class average, what should you do with it?

options.text: Leave it out, and say one mark is missing

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — leave it out and say so. A zero would pull the average down, and a filled-in mark would be invented.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a blank isn't a zero, and filling it in invents a mark. Leave it out and say one mark is missing.

checkpoints.prompt: A batch has one bad reading among twenty good ones. Which choice keeps the good data moving?

options.text: Set the bad row aside to check

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the twenty good readings go on to the report, and the bad one waits for a person to fix it.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — stopping loses twenty good readings, and letting everything through spoils the report. Set the bad row aside.
